title: Sensitive GPS data collection
description: Live GPS coordinates are highly sensitive personal data that may be collected without strict necessity assessment

title: Excessive frequency of data transmission
description: Regular interval GPS transmissions may be more frequent than functionally needed for the system's purpose

title: Fine-grained location data disclosure
description: Live GPS coordinates provide fine-grained location granularity that may exceed functional requirements

title: Revealing location attributes
description: GPS coordinates are revealing attributes that can be used to identify and track the data subject's movements

title: Individual distinguishability through GPS
description: Live GPS coordinates can make the individual distinguishable from others, reducing anonymity

title: Linking through quasi-identifier (GPS)
description: GPS coordinates combined with other data (time, device ID) can serve as quasi-identifiers to link to specific individuals

title: Profiling through movement patterns
description: GPS data can be analyzed to profile individual movement patterns and behaviors

title: Unawareness of continuous tracking
description: The child data subject may not be aware that their GPS location is being continuously tracked and processed

title: Lack of control over data processing
description: The child may not have control over how, when, and for how long their GPS data is processed

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: GPS data may be more personal data than actually needed for the system's functional goals

title: Insufficient data subject controls
description: Support for data subject rights regarding GPS data (access, rectification, erasure) may be lacking

title: Location-based linking through unique identifiers
description: Location pings from mobile app backend can be used to link user identity across sessions or devices, enabling tracking of individual movement patterns.

title: Quasi-identifier combining for linking
description: Location data combined with other user data (device ID, time, etc.) can serve as quasi-identifiers to link data across different sources.

title: Processing of identified location data
description: Location pings are identified personal data being processed and forwarded to geofencing engine for zone checking.

title: Location data as unique identifier
description: Location pings can serve as unique references to identify specific users and their movements.

title: Sensitive location data type
description: Location data is highly sensitive personal data that should only be collected and processed when strictly required for geofencing functionality.

title: Excessive volume of location data
description: All location pings may be forwarded regardless of whether they are needed for geofencing zone entry/exit detection.

title: Propagation to external service
description: Location data is propagated to the geofencing engine service where it may be accessible beyond the immediate functional need.

title: User unawareness of location processing
description: Users may not be aware that their location pings are being forwarded to the geofencing engine for processing.

title: Lack of user control over location data
description: Users may not have control to customize or opt-out of location data forwarding to the geofencing engine.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Location data may be processed in excess of what is actually needed for geofencing zone entry/exit functionality.

title: Data exposure to multiple parties
description: Location data is made accessible to the geofencing engine which may share with other parties beyond the immediate functional need.

title: Quasi-identifier combining data of a single individual
description: Zone definitions (home, school, friend's house) can serve as quasi-identifiers that, when combined with other data, could link to specific individuals.
assumptions: Zone data may be combined with other personal data to identify individuals.

title: Profiling an individual
description: Zone definitions can be analyzed to profile individuals' locations, habits, and routines, revealing patterns about their daily life.
assumptions: Zone data is collected and potentially analyzed for patterns.

title: Processing of identified data
description: The system processes zone definitions which may contain identified information about individuals' locations and preferences.
assumptions: Zone data contains identifiable information about individuals.

title: Data type sensitivity
description: Location-based zone definitions may be more sensitive than functionally required for the geofencing system's basic operation.
assumptions: Zone data includes location information that could be sensitive.

title: Amount
description: Zone definitions may include more location data than functionally needed for the geofencing alert functionality.
assumptions: All zone types (home, school, friend's house) may be collected even if only some are needed.

title: Unawareness as data subject
description: Users may not be aware that their zone definitions are being read and processed by the Geofencing Engine.
assumptions: Users may not understand the extent of data processing for geofencing.

title: Preferences
description: Users may lack control over which zone definitions are processed or how they are used by the geofencing system.
assumptions: Users may not have granular control over zone data processing.

title: Treatment, analysis, enrichment
description: The Geofencing Engine may analyze or enrich zone data beyond what is functionally needed for alert generation.
assumptions: Zone data may be analyzed for patterns or insights beyond basic geofencing.

title: Involved parties
description: Zone data may be made accessible to more parties than functionally necessary for the geofencing alert system.
assumptions: Zone data may be shared with additional services or parties beyond the core geofencing function.

title: Linking through unique identifier
description: Account data stored in DS2 contains unique identifiers that can link child profile and geofence zone data to specific individuals

title: Quasi-identifier combining data of a single individual
description: Combination of child profile attributes and geofence zone data can serve as quasi-identifiers that link to specific individuals

title: Profiling an individual
description: Analysis of account, child profile, and geofence zone data can enable profiling of individual users and their family members

title: Processing of identified data
description: The system requests and processes identified data including account information, child profiles, and geofence zones

title: Identifier
description: Account data contains unique references to the identity of the data subject stored in DS2

title: Revealing attributes
description: Child profile and geofence zone data include revealing attributes that support identification of data subjects

title: Data type sensitivity
description: Child profile and geofence zone data are highly sensitive and should only be collected when strictly required

title: Amount
description: Excessive amount of personal data may be processed beyond what is functionally needed for the system

title: Treatment, analysis, enrichment
description: Personal data may be further treated, analyzed, and enriched in ways not necessary for system functionality

title: Predetermined set of parties
description: Personal data is made accessible to more parties than functionally necessary

title: Unawareness as data subject
description: Data subjects may not be aware about the collection, storage, or disclosure of their personal data

title: Preferences
description: Lack of control of a data subject to set preferences or consent in how personal data is processed

title: Insufficient data subject controls
description: Support for different data subject rights (access, rectification, erasure) may be lacking

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: More personal data is processed than is actually needed for the system functionality

title: Location data used as identifier for child
description: Child's location data is processed and shared, which can serve as a unique reference to identify the child's identity and movements.
assumptions: Location data is collected and transmitted to the mobile app backend.

title: Location as revealing attribute
description: Location data is a revealing attribute that can be used to identify the child's whereabouts and potentially infer other personal information about the child.
assumptions: Location data is transmitted to the mobile app backend.

title: Data disclosed to more parties than functionally needed
description: Child's location data is shared with secondary guardians (grandparent, relative) who may not be functionally necessary for the core purpose of the system.
assumptions: The system allows sharing with any secondary guardian without strict functional necessity assessment.

title: Child unaware of location sharing
description: The child data subject may not be aware that their location is being collected and shared with secondary guardians.
assumptions: The child is a minor and may not have the capacity to understand or consent to location sharing.

title: Child lacks control over data sharing preferences
description: The child data subject has no control over which guardians can access their location data or how long it is retained.
assumptions: The system does not provide granular consent controls for the child.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Location data may be more personal data than actually needed for the functional purpose of sharing with a secondary guardian.
assumptions: The system collects and processes location data beyond what is strictly required for the sharing functionality.

title: Potential invalid consent for child data
description: Location data collection and sharing may not rely on valid consent from the child data subject if they are too young to provide meaningful consent.
assumptions: The child is a minor and the system does not obtain appropriate consent mechanisms.

title: Sensitive data type disclosed
description: Live location data is a highly sensitive personal data type that should only be shared when strictly required for the functional purpose of the system.

title: Fine-grained location data disclosed
description: Live location data is disclosed at a very fine-grained level of granularity, potentially revealing precise movement patterns and whereabouts of the child.

title: Data disclosed to external party
description: Personal data is being shared with an external party (secondary guardian) who is not part of the core system, increasing exposure beyond what may be functionally necessary.

title: Location data contains unique identifier
description: Live location data may contain unique references to the identity of the child, potentially allowing identification of the specific data subject.

title: Revealing attributes included
description: Live location data includes revealing attributes that support the identification of the data subject (the child).

title: Data subject unaware of processing
description: The child (data subject) may not be aware that their live location is being shared with a secondary guardian, violating their right to know about data processing.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Live location data may be more personal data than is actually needed for the functional purpose of the system, violating the data minimization principle.

title: Potential unlawful processing
description: Sharing live location data with a secondary guardian may not rely on valid consent or may lack proper lawful ground, potentially constituting unlawful processing.

title: Data shared with external advertising partner
description: Aggregated usage and engagement analytics are shared with an external advertising/analytics partner (EE4), which is a party not functionally necessary for the core app functionality.
assumptions: The advertising partner is a predetermined, known party, but the data is being shared beyond what is strictly required for the app's primary function.

title: Potentially sensitive data types disclosed
description: Usage and engagement analytics may include data types that are more sensitive than functionally required for the app's core functionality.
assumptions: Aggregated analytics may contain behavioral patterns that could be sensitive even if not individually identifiable.

title: Profiling of individuals through engagement patterns
description: Aggregated usage and engagement analytics can be analyzed to identify patterns that may link back to specific individuals, especially when combined with other data sources.
assumptions: The aggregation may not be truly anonymous and could be used for profiling purposes.

title: Potential re-identification through small anonymity sets
description: If the aggregated analytics are based on small user groups or specific behaviors, the anonymity set may be too small, allowing singling out of individual data subjects.
assumptions: The granularity of the aggregated data may not provide sufficient anonymity.

title: Excessive location data collection
description: Current location data may be more sensitive than functionally required for a simple check-in/SOS message, potentially including GPS coordinates, timestamp, and device information beyond what's needed for the emergency function.

title: Fine-grained location granularity
description: Location data disclosed may be at a fine-grained level (exact coordinates) rather than a broader area, which could enable more precise tracking than necessary for a check-in/SOS function.

title: Data exposure to multiple parties
description: Location data from the child may be accessible to more parties than functionally necessary (e.g., parent, emergency services, analytics systems) beyond the intended SOS/check-in recipient.

title: Processing of unique identifier
description: The mobile app backend processes location data that may contain unique references to the child's identity, potentially enabling identification through device identifiers or account linkage.

title: Revealing attributes in data
description: The SOS/check-in message may include revealing attributes (device ID, account information, time-stamped location) that support identification of the data subject beyond the intended purpose.

title: Unawareness of data processing
description: The child data subject may not be fully aware that their location data is being collected, processed, and potentially stored beyond the immediate SOS/check-in function.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: More personal data (location, device info, timestamps) may be processed than is actually needed for the functional goal of a simple check-in/SOS message.

title: Attributable data evidence
description: The SOS/check-in message can be attributed to the child, which may prevent the child from denying certain claims about their location or actions.
